### Version Checks (indicate both or one)

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the lastest [release](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/releases) of PyPSA.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the current [`master`](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/tree/master) branch of PyPSA.


### Issue Description

Since the release Pypsa 0.32.0, all the extendable generators are not in the list when I do the statistics command: expanded_capacity(comps='Generator', groupby=False) or  optimal_capacity(comps='Generator', groupby=False)

When I execute the same command with pypsa 0.31, all works fine, I have the expanded capacity of extendable generators.
      

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pypsa
n = pypsa.Network()
stats = self.n.statistics
expanded_capacity = stats.expanded_capacity(comps='Generator', groupby=False).fillna(0)
```

### Expected Behavior

expanded_capacity should contain the expanded capacity for all generators but when I look the list, there is only the ones with p_nom_extendable = False and not the extendable generators.

hints_text:
Please provide a reproducible example. Your example yields an empty list in any case.
Finally, the bug is not linked with the parameter "extendable" but with the build_year. Since pypsa 0.32.0, when you use the statistics function, only the generators/storage_units (and probably line/links too) built at the "start_year" or before are considered. If you execute the code below, you will see that only "gen1" and "su1" are in the list of "expanded_capacity":

### Code to execute
```python
import pypsa
import pandas as pd
n = pypsa.examples.ac_dc_meshed(from_master=True)
n.add(
    "Generator",
    "gen1",
    bus="Manchester",
    build_year = 2020)
n.add(
    "Generator",
    "gen2",
    bus="Manchester",
    build_year = 2021)
n.add(
    "Generator",
    "gen3",
    bus="Manchester",
    build_year = 2030)
n.add(
    "StorageUnit",
    "su1",
    bus="Manchester",
    build_year = 2020)
n.add(
    "StorageUnit",
    "su2",
    bus="Manchester",
    build_year = 2050)
years = [2020, 2030, 2040, 2050]
freq = "24"

snapshots = pd.DatetimeIndex([])
for year in years:
    period = pd.date_range(
        start=f"{year}-01-01 00:00",
        freq=f"{freq}H",
        periods=8760 / float(freq),
    )
    snapshots = snapshots.append(period)

# convert to multiindex and assign to network
n.snapshots = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays([snapshots.year, snapshots])
n.investment_periods = years
n.optimize(multi_investment_periods=True)

stats = n.statistics
print(stats.expanded_capacity(comps='Generator', groupby=False).fillna(0))
print(stats.expanded_capacity(comps='StorageUnit', groupby=False).fillna(0))
```
Hello @lkstrp , Is there somebody on the subject? I haven't managed to solve the problem on my side...


Thanks for reporting that issue @adpr1. Even though it took us a while to drill down into it, we were able to uncover a serious regression we introduced in version 0.32 thanks to you.

Sorry for the wait, a bugfix release will follow in the coming days.
